subject: A survey plan seen from overhead in which the row lies along a dashed datum on a grid and a bright release board holds every bob on one line, ready to snake across it.
controls: length: the span of every bob's lane across the datum, and so how far the board sits from it (position/scale, ~38 to 70 px).
count: how many lanes cross the datum (count, 3 to 16).
swing: the size of each bob's proportional symbol, how hard it will cross (scale, 3 to 7 px radius).
scale: which ticks stand tall on the two-octave strip along the bottom, with each pendulum's note marked above its tick (count and position in the strip).
muted: The release board comes back down onto the bobs wherever they are and the strip's marks go hollow: held, not playing.
risks: Seen from above the pendulum's length is invisible, so length borrows the lane span (which physically also grows with swing); swing is then a symbol size, a map convention rather than a physical part. The grid is ground decoration and costs nothing, but it is the most 'chart-like' of the five.
